passage: Note, Wednesday, by Pema, Maths teacher. Pranav stayed after class with his failed test and said, "I will find out why myself." He wrote on the board: Why did I fail? Because I could not solve the equations. Why? Because I got the algebra steps wrong. Why? Because I do not handle negative signs and brackets well. Why? Because my Class 8 basics in fractions and algebra are weak. Why did I skip those? Because I passed Class 8 and never went back. He turned and said, "It is not this chapter. It is the foundation." I added nothing. I offered him Class 8 practice sheets, and he took two.

qa.q: What did Pranav conclude was the root of the problem?
qa.a: He concluded that the weak fractions and algebra basics from Class 8 were the root.

qa.q: What might Pranav have felt when he reached the last "why"?
qa.a: Relieved to find a fixable cause, though perhaps uncomfortable about having skipped the basics.
Work through Class 8 practice sheets in short sessions, then return to the current chapter, because the foundation supports it.

qa.q: How might Pema see Pranav's self-analysis?
qa.a: As a strong sign of ownership, since Pema added nothing and only offered practice sheets.

grounding: A student failing Maths asks why repeatedly and traces the trouble back to weak Class 8 basics, not the current chapter.

passage:
Tuesday
Got 21 out of 80 in the Maths unit test. Again. Binita Ma'am said, "Ask yourself why, and keep asking." So tonight I tried it.
Why did I fail? Couldn't do the quadratic questions.
Why? Kept getting the factorising wrong.
Why? The minus signs and fractions mess me up.
Why? I never really got how negatives and fractions work with letters.
Why? Class 8. I copied the algebra homework from Sonu all year because I didn't understand it and was too scared to ask.
So it's not quadratics. It's Class 8. I've been building on a hole. Weirdly, that's a relief. Tomorrow I'm finding my old Class 8 book and starting with fractions, even if it feels babyish.
Pradeep

qa.q: What did Pradeep score in the Maths unit test?
Why does Pradeep find the answer a relief?
qa.a: Pradeep feels relieved because the problem finally has a clear, fixable cause, gaps from Class 8, rather than being hopeless at Maths.

qa.q: What would you add to Pradeep's plan?
qa.a: Tell Binita Ma'am about the Class 8 gap, so she can suggest which basics to practise first and check progress.

qa.q: How might Binita Ma'am feel if Pradeep shares this?
qa.a: Binita Ma'am would likely be pleased that the advice worked and that the real gap is now known, making it easier to help.

grounding: A student's diary traces a failing Maths grade through repeated whys back to weak Class 8 fractions and algebra.
